notes: M07-05 own-dependency review. Records every external surface this implementation actually depends on, why it is acceptable in a minimal stack, and how it is isolated. Native surfaces are called out because they are the hardest to replace. There is no package-manager dependency graph here: the toolchain is pinned, the OS tools are named, and nothing is fetched at runtime except through the guarded transport.

dependencies.isolation: build-time only; not present in produced binaries
dependencies.update_procedure: bump pinned rev, rebuild, run tools/check.sh; no `latest` in automation

dependencies.isolation: only through a small declared extern set (system, mkdir, getenv, time, socket/fd calls) in rh_base and rh_http
dependencies.update_procedure: externs are minimal and documented; a libc change is caught by the suite

dependencies.pinned: version captured into every scan's evidence (git-version.txt)
dependencies.isolation: invoked only via allowlisted arguments; plumbing commands only
dependencies.update_procedure: tool version is evidenced per scan; a format change fails the log parse rather than producing wrong numbers

dependencies.pinned: no version pin; flags are constants
dependencies.isolation: proto restricted to https+file, redirects disabled, byte/time caps, no auth header
dependencies.update_procedure: flag set is fixed in rh_git; a change requires re-running the transport tests

dependencies.isolation: used by tools/*.sh checks only, never by the Elisa product or live path
dependencies.update_procedure: checks are simple stdlib scripts; a break is caught immediately by tools/check.sh

rules: runtime network access only through the guarded transport, never from metrics or policy
no package manager resolves dependencies at build or run time
native surfaces (libc) are the smallest declared extern set and are named here
an added dependency requires an update to this review and an ADR if it changes the stack
not_covered: no transitive package SBOM is produced because there is no package manager in the stack
OS tool versions other than git are not evidenced per run
